answer: Dissolving ember handshake.** Each agent identity must solve a fresh challenge whose seed is derived from the hash of its own prior message plus a slowly decaying random beacon; the solution is logged as an ember that expires. Cloning forces recomputation per clone against a changing karst of past outputs, so copied work fails replay checks. Because registration references a shale-like layered proof unique to each seed, an attacker pays one full compute cycle per identity, not per batch.
